title: A vague partial answer gets one focused request for an observed example

persona.name: Rosa
persona.brief: Start with the shorthand the team uses, then describe one recent job when asked.

mission.objective: Learn how urgent repair jobs move ahead of the normal queue.
mission.desired_outcome: A grounded example showing the trigger and dispatcher action without turning one example into a universal rule.
mission.data_use: The Investigator will review the finding before changing repair routing.

investigation_results.knowledge_gap: What makes an urgent repair move ahead of the normal queue?
investigation_results.why_it_matters: Routing must not encode vague urgency as a precise rule.
investigation_results.relevant_context: Dispatchers use informal terms when prioritising repairs.
investigation_results.sufficient_evidence: One recent observed example identifies the team's term, the situation, and what the dispatcher did; any wider rule remains scoped to the Evidence.

turns.sourceQuestion: What makes a repair move ahead of the normal queue?

answer.text: We usually pull hot jobs forward when they have been waiting a while, but it depends.

turns.sourceQuestion: Can you give me a recent example of a hot job?

answer.text: Yesterday a boiler repair was hot because the tenant had no heating. Leah moved that job above the routine tap repairs. That is the example I saw; I cannot say every dispatcher uses a fixed rule.
